items.en: The Marks of Internal Wholesome Roots Arising: The Contemplation of Impurity
items.zh: 內善根發相 · 不淨觀門

zh: 二、明不淨觀中有三種善根發相不同：一、九想；二、背捨；三、大不淨觀。一、九想善根者，亦於欲界、未到靜定心中，忽然見他男女死屍胮脹，爾時其心驚悟，自傷往昔惛迷，厭患所愛五欲，永不親近；或見青瘀、血塗、膿爛，噉殘狼藉，白骨散壞等相。此為九想善根發相。
en: Second, clarifying that the contemplation of impurity has three differing marks of wholesome roots arising: the nine contemplations; the liberations; and the great contemplation of impurity.

First, the wholesome root of the nine contemplations: likewise, within the still concentration of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, one suddenly sees the swollen corpse of some man or woman; at that moment the mind is startled awake, grieving over its own past confusion and delusion, and grows disgusted with the five desires it once loved, never to draw near them again; or one sees marks of livid discoloration, blood-smeared flesh, festering pus, gnawed and scattered remains, and scattered, decaying white bones. This is the mark of the nine contemplations' wholesome root arising.

zh: 二、明背捨善根發者，亦於欲界、未到靜定心中，忽見內身不淨、胮脹、狼藉；或見自身白骨，從頭至足，節節相拄，乃至骨人光明昱燿，定心安隱，厭患五欲，不著我人。此是背捨善根發相。
en: Second, clarifying the arising of the wholesome root of the liberations: likewise, within the still concentration of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, one suddenly sees one's own inner body impure, swollen, and scattered; or one sees one's own white bones, from head to foot, joint propping joint, until the skeleton itself gleams with light — the concentrated mind at peace, disgusted with the five desires, no longer attached to self or person. This is the mark of the liberations' wholesome root arising.

zh: 三、明大不淨觀善根發者，亦於欲界、未到定心中，見於內身及外身、一切飛禽走獸、衣服、飲食、山林、樹木皆悉不淨，或見一家、一聚落、一國土，乃至十方，皆悉不淨；或見白骨，乃至見自身白骨光明昱燿等。此為大不淨觀勝處善根發相。此觀發時，能破一切著心。
en: Third, clarifying the arising of the wholesome root of the great contemplation of impurity: likewise, within the concentration of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, one sees one's own body and the bodies of others, and every flying bird and running beast, every garment, every food and drink, every mountain forest and tree, all of it equally impure; or one sees a single household, a single village, a single land, and, further still, the ten directions, all of it equally impure; or one sees white bones, down to one's own white bones gleaming with light. This is the mark of the wholesome root of the great contemplation of impurity and the stations of mastery arising. When this contemplation arises, it is able to break through every attached mind.

The progression from the nine contemplations to the liberations to the great contemplation of impurity mirrors the earth-water-wind-golden sand-vajra progression of the five wheels earlier in this fascicle: each stage takes what the last one saw and extends it — from a single corpse, to one's own body reduced to bone, to the entire visible world seen as equally impure, ending in a scope wide enough to dissolve attachment itself rather than merely one object of desire.

items.en: The Marks of Internal Wholesome Roots Arising: Loving-Kindness
items.zh: 內善根發相 · 慈心門

zh: 三、明慈心觀中三種善根發不同者：一、眾生緣慈；二、法緣慈；三、無緣慈。一、眾生緣慈發者，亦於欲界、未到靜定心中，忽然發心，慈念眾生，先緣親人得樂之相，因發定，安隱快樂，乃至中人、怨人悉見得樂，無瞋無恨，無怨無惱，廣大無量，遍滿十方。是為眾生緣慈善根發相。或發眾生緣悲，乃至喜、捨亦如是。
en: Third, clarifying that the contemplation of loving-kindness has three differing marks of wholesome roots arising: loving-kindness that takes sentient beings as its object; loving-kindness that takes dharma as its object; and objectless loving-kindness.

First, the arising of loving-kindness that takes sentient beings as its object: likewise, within the still concentration of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, the mind suddenly arises, holding sentient beings in loving-kindness — first taking the mark of a loved one's happiness as its object, and, through this, concentration is brought forth, peaceful and joyful, until even neutral persons and enemies are all seen gaining happiness, without anger, without resentment, without enmity, without vexation, vast and measureless, filling all ten directions. This is the mark of loving-kindness that takes sentient beings as its object arising. Compassion that takes sentient beings as its object may likewise arise, and joy and equanimity in the same way.

zh: 二、明法緣慈發者，亦於欲界、未到靜定心中，忽然自覺一切內外但有陰入法，起唯法起，滅唯法滅，不見眾生及我、我所，但有五陰，於受陰中有樂受。如是知已，即緣此樂受發於慈定，無瞋無恨，無怨無惱，廣大無量，遍滿十方，是為法緣慈。或發法緣悲，乃至喜、捨，亦如慈善根發相。
en: Second, clarifying the arising of loving-kindness that takes dharma as its object: likewise, within the still concentration of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, one suddenly becomes aware that everything, within and without, is nothing but the dharma of the aggregates and sense-bases — what arises, only dharma arises; what ceases, only dharma ceases — and one no longer sees any sentient being, self, or what belongs to a self, but only the five aggregates, and, within the aggregate of sensation, a pleasant sensation. Having come to know this, one takes this very pleasant sensation as the object from which loving-kindness-concentration is brought forth, without anger, without resentment, without enmity, without vexation, vast and measureless, filling all ten directions — this is loving-kindness that takes dharma as its object. Compassion that takes dharma as its object may likewise arise, and joy and equanimity, following the same pattern as loving-kindness's wholesome root arising.

zh: 三、明無緣慈發者，亦於欲界、未到定心中，忽然覺悟一切諸法非有非無，不見二邊，所謂若眾生非眾生，若法非法，皆不可得，則無所緣，以無緣故，顛倒想息，寂然安樂，心與慈定相應，等觀一切，同此安樂，無瞋無恨，無怨無惱，廣大無量，遍滿十方，是為無緣慈善根發相。或發無緣悲定，乃至喜、捨亦如是。
en: Third, clarifying the arising of objectless loving-kindness: likewise, within the concentration of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, one suddenly awakens to the fact that no dharma whatsoever is either existent or nonexistent, and one no longer sees either of the two extremes — that is, whether "sentient being" or "not a sentient being," whether "dharma" or "not a dharma," none of it can be found, and so there is nothing at all to take as an object. Because there is no object, inverted thinking comes to rest, still and at ease, and the mind accords with loving-kindness-concentration, viewing all things equally, all of it sharing in this same ease, without anger, without resentment, without enmity, without vexation, vast and measureless, filling all ten directions — this is the mark of objectless loving-kindness's wholesome root arising. Objectless compassion-concentration may likewise arise, and joy and equanimity in the same way.

The three-object scheme for loving-kindness (sentient beings, dharma, and no object at all) directly parallels the gate of stopping's own three kinds — fixed-object, restraining-the-mind, and embodying-truth — moving the same way from a concrete object of attention, to a doctrinally refined object (the aggregates rather than a "person"), to the collapse of the subject-object structure altogether. Each of the four immeasurable minds (loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity) is said to follow the identical three-stage pattern, though only loving-kindness is worked out in full here.

items.en: The Marks of Internal Wholesome Roots Arising: Causation
items.zh: 內善根發相 · 因緣門

zh: 四、明因緣觀中有三種善根發不同者：一、三世十二緣；二、果報十二緣；三、一念十二緣。一、明三世十二因緣善根發者，亦於欲界、未到定心中，忽然覺悟心生，推尋三世，過去無明以來，不見我、人、無明等法，不斷不常，能破六十二種諸邪見網，心得正定，安隱寂然，觀慧分明，通達無礙，身口清淨，正行成就，此是三世十二因緣觀慧善根發相。
en: Fourth, clarifying that the contemplation of causation has three differing marks of wholesome roots arising: the twelve links across the three periods of time; the twelve links as karmic result; and the twelve links within a single thought-moment.

First, clarifying the arising of the wholesome root of the twelve links across the three periods of time: likewise, within the concentration of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, the awakened mind suddenly arises, tracing back through the three periods of time — from ignorance in the past onward — and one no longer sees any dharma such as a self, a person, or ignorance itself; seeing neither annihilation nor permanence, one is able thereby to break through the net of sixty-two kinds of wrong views. The mind attains right concentration, at peace and still, contemplative wisdom clear, penetrating without obstruction, body and speech pure, right conduct accomplished. This is the mark of the wholesome root of contemplative wisdom regarding the twelve links across the three periods of time arising.

zh: 二、明果報十二因緣善根發者，亦於欲界、未到定心中，忽覺心識明利，即自思尋：「我初生時，攬父母身分以為己有，名歌羅邏。歌羅邏時，名曰無明，因緣則有行、識，乃至老死，名為十二因緣。若歌羅邏時，但有三事合和，無人無我，三事不實。今無明等十二因緣諸法，竟何所依？若不見無明等諸法定是有者，豈是無邪？」如是念時，破有、無二見，歸心正道，正定相應，慧解開發，離諸邪行，此為果報十二因緣觀智善根發相。如此明十二因緣，出《大集經》中具辨。作此明因緣相，與苦集正同，亦得約此明四諦善根發也。
en: Second, clarifying the arising of the wholesome root of the twelve links as karmic result: likewise, within the concentration of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, one suddenly becomes aware that mind and consciousness have grown clear and sharp, and reflects directly: "When I was first born, I took hold of a portion of my parents' bodies and made it my own — this is called kalala. At the time of kalala, this is named ignorance; through causes and conditions there is then formation, consciousness, and so on up through old age and death — this is called the twelve links. But at the time of kalala, there was only the coming together of three things, with no person and no self in it at all — the three things themselves are not real. Now, ignorance and the other dharmas of the twelve links — on what, in the end, do they actually depend? And if ignorance and the other dharmas are not seen to definitely exist, how could they be said to definitely not exist either?" Reflecting in this way, one breaks through the two views of existence and nonexistence, the mind returning to the correct path, according with right concentration; wisdom and understanding are brought forth, and every deviant conduct is left behind. This is the mark of the wholesome root of contemplative knowledge regarding the twelve links as karmic result arising. This account of the twelve links is given in full in the Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra. What is clarified here as the mark of causation is exactly the same as suffering and its accumulation, and the arising of the Four Noble Truths' own wholesome root may likewise be clarified along these same lines.

zh: 三、明一念十二因緣善根發者，亦於欲界、未到靜定心中，忽然自覺剎那之心，無人無我，性本無實。所以者何？一念起時，必藉因緣，言因緣者，即具十二因緣，緣無自性，一念豈有定實？若不得一念之實，即破世性邪執，心與正定相應，智慧開發，猶如涌泉，身口清淨，離諸邪行，是為一念十二緣善根發相。此之十二因緣，亦出《大集經》中具辨，亦得約此十二緣明一心具四諦善根發也。
en: Third, clarifying the arising of the wholesome root of the twelve links within a single thought-moment: likewise, within the still concentration of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, one suddenly becomes aware that the mind of a single instant has no person and no self in it, its very nature originally without reality. Why is this? Whenever a single thought arises, it necessarily depends on causes and conditions; and what is meant by causes and conditions here is precisely the twelve links in full — and since conditions have no nature of their own, how could a single thought-moment possibly have any fixed reality? Once the reality of a single thought-moment can no longer be found, the deviant grasping at a fixed worldly nature is thereby broken through; the mind accords with right concentration, and wisdom is brought forth as though gushing from a spring, body and speech pure, every deviant conduct left behind. This is the mark of the twelve links within a single thought-moment's wholesome root arising. This account of the twelve links, too, is given in full in the Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra, and the arising of the Four Noble Truths' own wholesome root, complete within a single mind, may likewise be clarified along these same twelve links.

The kalala reference deliberately recalls fascicle 1's own three-part account of conception, quoted there from the same Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra — the treatise circling back to reuse a passage already established rather than introducing new source material. All three approaches to the twelve links converge on the identical conclusion reached by fascicle 3's earlier tetralemma against "karma cannot be found": neither a fixed self nor a fixed absence of self can be located, whether the analysis spans three lifetimes, a single conception, or a single thought-moment. The explicit equation with the Four Noble Truths (dependent origination's arising = suffering and its accumulation, the first two truths) is a reminder that this whole apparatus of analysis, however elaborate, is meant to converge on the same handful of truths taught throughout the tradition.

items.en: The Marks of Internal Wholesome Roots Arising: Buddha-Recollection
items.zh: 內善根發相 · 念佛門

zh: 五、明念佛中自有三種善根發相不同：一、念應佛；二、念報佛；三、念法佛。明三佛義，出《楞伽經》廣分別其相也。一、明念應佛善根發者，亦於欲界、未到靜定心中，忽然憶念佛之功德，即作是念：「如來往昔阿僧祇劫中，為一切眾生故，備行六波羅蜜，一切功德智慧故，身有相好光明，心有智慧圓照，降伏魔怨，無師自悟，自覺覺他，轉正法輪，普度一切，乃至入涅槃後，舍利經教廣益眾生。如是等功德，無量無邊。」作是念時，即敬愛心生，三昧開發，入定安樂，或於定中見佛身相，善心開發，或聞佛說法，心淨信解。如是等勝善境界非一，是為念應佛善根發相。
en: Fifth, clarifying that buddha-recollection has three differing marks of wholesome roots arising: recollecting the response-body buddha; recollecting the reward-body buddha; and recollecting the dharma-body buddha. The meaning of these three buddha-bodies is given in full detail in the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra.

First, clarifying the arising of the wholesome root of recollecting the response-body buddha: likewise, within the still concentration of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, one suddenly recalls the Buddha's own merit, and reflects: "Throughout innumerable asaṃkhyeya kalpas in the past, the Tathāgata, for the sake of all sentient beings, fully practiced the six pāramitās; because of every merit and every wisdom, his body possesses the excellent marks and radiant light, his mind possesses wisdom that illuminates all things completely; he subdued demons and enemies, awakened of himself without a teacher, awakened himself and awakened others, turned the wheel of the true Dharma, and brought universal salvation to all — and even after entering nirvāṇa, his relics and his teachings continue broadly to benefit sentient beings. Such merits as these are measureless and boundless." Reflecting in this way, a mind of reverence and love at once arises, samādhi is brought forth, and one enters concentration in peace and joy; or, within concentration, one sees the Buddha's own bodily form, and a wholesome mind is brought forth; or one hears the Buddha expounding the Dharma, the mind pure with faith and understanding. Such excellent, wholesome states as these are not of one kind only — this is the mark of recollecting the response-body buddha's wholesome root arising.

zh: 二、明念報佛善根發者，亦於欲界、未到靜細心中，忽然憶念：「十方諸佛真實圓滿果報之身，湛然常住，色心清淨，微妙寂滅，功德智慧充滿法界，不生不滅，無作無為，豈有王宮之生，亦非雙樹之滅，為化眾生，十方佛土普應生滅。如是等功德無量無邊，不可思議。」作是念時，心定安隱，三昧開發，慧解分明。或作定中見不可思議佛法境界，即便出生無量願行、無量功德、無量智慧三昧法門，是為念報佛善根發相。
en: Second, clarifying the arising of the wholesome root of recollecting the reward-body buddha: likewise, within the still, fine mind of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, one suddenly recalls: "The true and perfectly complete reward-body of every buddha in the ten directions abides forever, deep and unmoving; form and mind alike pure, subtle and still; merit and wisdom filling the entire dharma-realm; neither arising nor ceasing, neither fabricated nor conditioned. How, then, could there truly be a birth in a royal palace, or truly a passing away between twin trees? It is only for the sake of transforming sentient beings that they respond universally throughout the buddha-lands of the ten directions, manifesting arising and ceasing. Such merits as these are measureless, boundless, and inconceivable." Reflecting in this way, the mind becomes concentrated and at peace, samādhi is brought forth, understanding clear. Or, within concentration, one beholds inconceivable dharma-states of the Buddha, and thereupon measureless vows and practices, measureless merit, and measureless wisdom-samādhi dharma-gates are brought forth — this is the mark of recollecting the reward-body buddha's wholesome root arising.

zh: 三、明念法佛善根發者，亦於欲界、未到靜定心中，忽然憶念：「十方諸佛法身實相，猶如虛空。」即便覺悟一切諸法本自不生，今則無滅，非有非無，非來非去，非增非減，非境非智，非因非果，非常非斷，非縛非脫，非生死非涅槃，湛然清淨，有佛無佛，相性常然，眾生、諸佛同一實相者，即是法身佛也。故《大品經》云：「諸法如實相。」諸法如實即是佛，離是之外，更無別佛。如是念時，三昧現前，實慧開發，即時通達無量法門，寂然不動，一切不思議境界皆現定中成就之相。如《法華經》六根清淨中廣說，是為念法佛善根發相。
en: Third, clarifying the arising of the wholesome root of recollecting the dharma-body buddha: likewise, within the still concentration of the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, one suddenly recalls: "The true mark of every buddha's dharma-body in the ten directions is just like empty space." One thereupon awakens to the fact that every dharma is, in itself, originally unarisen, and so now has no cessation either — neither existent nor nonexistent, neither coming nor going, neither increasing nor decreasing, neither object nor knowing subject, neither cause nor effect, neither permanent nor cut off, neither bound nor liberated, neither birth-and-death nor nirvāṇa, deep and pure; whether a buddha appears or not, the mark of this nature remains forever the same — sentient beings and every buddha share this one and the same true mark, and this is precisely the dharma-body buddha. Hence the Larger Sūtra says: "The true mark of every dharma, just as it is." Every dharma, just as it truly is, is itself the Buddha — apart from this, there is no separate buddha to be found. Reflecting in this way, samādhi manifests before one, and true wisdom is brought forth; measureless dharma-gates are penetrated at once, still and unmoving, every inconceivable state manifesting, within concentration, as an accomplished mark. This is given in full in the purification of the six sense-faculties in the Lotus Sūtra — this is the mark of recollecting the dharma-body buddha's wholesome root arising.

The three-body scheme (response, reward, dharma) runs through the identical coarse-to-fine progression already seen twice this fascicle — a concrete devotional object (the Buddha's biography and physical marks), a more refined but still positively-described object (a reward-body abiding eternally, filling the dharma-realm), and finally an object with no positive content left to grasp at all (a dharma-body described entirely through negation, "neither... nor," collapsing the very distinction between buddha and non-buddha). That this is placed last among the five internal gates, and that fascicle 2 already called buddha-recollection's merit "vast and expansive... practiced by bodhisattvas," is consistent: the treatise consistently ranks its schemes from the concrete toward the empty, and buddha-recollection turns out to run the entire span in miniature.

quiz.q: What are the three marks of wholesome roots in the gate of impurity?
options: the nine contemplations, the liberations, the great contemplation of impurity
quiz.why: "The contemplation of impurity has three differing marks of wholesome roots arising: the nine contemplations; the liberations; and the great contemplation of impurity."

quiz.q: How do the nine contemplations and the liberations differ in what one sees?
options: nine contemplations: another's swollen corpse; liberations: one's own impure body or white skeleton, joint propping joint, until it gleams
quiz.why: In the nine contemplations "one suddenly sees the swollen corpse of some man or woman"; in the liberations "one suddenly sees one's own inner body impure ... or one sees one's own white bones, from head to foot, joint propping joint, until the skeleton itself gleams with light."

quiz.q: What does the great contemplation of impurity accomplish when it arises?
options: seeing everything within, without, and in the ten directions as impure, it breaks through every attached mind
quiz.why: "Or one sees a single household, a single village, a single land, and, further still, the ten directions, all of it equally impure ... When this contemplation arises, it is able to break through every attached mind."

quiz.q: What are the three kinds in the gate of loving-kindness, and with whom does loving-kindness toward beings begin?
options: small, middle, great; the Buddha first
toward beings, toward dharma, objectless; first a loved one's happiness, then neutral persons and enemies
quiz.why: "Loving-kindness that takes sentient beings as its object; loving-kindness that takes dharma as its object; and objectless loving-kindness ... first taking the mark of a loved one's happiness as its object ... until even neutral persons and enemies are all seen gaining happiness."

quiz.q: What does loving-kindness toward dharma take as its object?
options: seeing only aggregates and sense-bases, no being or self, it takes the pleasant sensation within the aggregate of sensation as object
quiz.why: "One no longer sees any sentient being, self, or what belongs to a self, but only the five aggregates, and, within the aggregate of sensation, a pleasant sensation. Having come to know this, one takes this very pleasant sensation as the object from which loving-kindness-concentration is brought forth."

options: because one does not wish to be kind
awakening that no dharma is existent or nonexistent, being and non-being, dharma and non-dharma all unfindable, there is nothing to take as object
quiz.why: "One suddenly awakens to the fact that no dharma whatsoever is either existent or nonexistent ... whether 'sentient being' or 'not a sentient being,' whether 'dharma' or 'not a dharma,' none of it can be found, and so there is nothing at all to take as an object."

quiz.q: What are the three wholesome roots in the gate of causation?
options: the twelve links across three times, as karmic result, within a single thought
quiz.why: "The contemplation of causation has three differing marks of wholesome roots arising: the twelve links across the three periods of time; the twelve links as karmic result; and the twelve links within a single thought-moment."

quiz.q: When the wholesome root of the twelve links across three times arises, what does it break through?
options: the net of sixty-two wrong views
quiz.why: "Tracing back through the three periods of time ... one no longer sees any dharma such as a self, a person, or ignorance itself as either cut off or permanent, able thereby to break through the net of sixty-two kinds of wrong views."

quiz.q: In the twelve links as karmic result, what is present at the kalala stage, and what views are broken?
options: only three things combined, with no person or self, and the three unreal; breaking the views of existence and nonexistence
quiz.why: "At the time of kalala, there was only the coming together of three things, with no person and no self in it at all — the three things themselves are not real ... Reflecting in this way, one breaks through the two views of existence and nonexistence."

quiz.q: Why does the twelve links within a single thought say a single thought has no fixed reality?
options: because a thought is too brief
every thought depends on causes and conditions, the full twelve links; conditions have no nature of their own, so how could one thought be fixed?
quiz.why: "Whenever a single thought arises, it necessarily depends on causes and conditions; and what is meant by causes and conditions here is precisely the twelve links in full — and since conditions have no nature of their own, how could a single thought-moment possibly have any fixed reality?"

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of buddha-recollection, and where is the meaning of the three buddhas given in full?
options: past, present, future buddhas; the Lotus
response-body, reward-body, dharma-body; the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra
quiz.why: "Recollecting the response-body buddha; recollecting the reward-body buddha; and recollecting the dharma-body buddha. The meaning of these three buddha-bodies is given in full detail in the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra."

quiz.q: What does the practitioner recall when recollecting the response-body buddha?
options: the Tathāgata's practice of the six perfections over countless kalpas, his marks and light, subduing demons, turning the wheel, and benefiting beings through relics and teachings after nirvāṇa
quiz.why: "Throughout innumerable asaṃkhyeya kalpas in the past, the Tathāgata, for the sake of all sentient beings, fully practiced the six pāramitās ... and even after entering nirvāṇa, his relics and his teachings continue broadly to benefit sentient beings."

quiz.q: In recollecting the reward-body buddha, the text says there is no true birth in a palace or passing between twin trees. What, then, are these?
options: the dharma body's birth and death
manifestations of arising and ceasing throughout the ten directions to transform beings
the reward body's real birth and death
quiz.why: The reward body abides forever, "neither arising nor ceasing ... How, then, could there truly be a birth in a royal palace, or truly a passing away between twin trees?" They are responses for transforming beings.

quiz.q: In recollecting the dharma-body buddha, what does the text, citing the Larger Sūtra, say is the Buddha?
options: the Buddha is the reward body
every dharma just as it truly is, is the Buddha; apart from this there is no other buddha
the Buddha is in the Western Pure Land
quiz.why: "Hence the Larger Sūtra says: 'The true mark of every dharma, just as it is.' Every dharma, just as it truly is, is itself the Buddha — apart from this, there is no separate buddha to be found."
